aj: Heads-up: saw a burst of preemptions in eu-west-1 yesterday around 03:10 UTC impacting low-priority training queues. +12% tail latency on worker allocs. Anyone else see it?

maria: yup saw it on the dashboard, odd price spikes but capacity looked healthy otherwise. logs show a wave of NodeTerminated events.

aj: digging into the procurement planner — our price-optimized pools bid down a lot during 03:00-03:30; maybe we got out-bid and then drained. Thinking of a temporal-smoothing bid layer to avoid reactive swings.

sachin: temporal smoothing = spread bids across a short horizon instead of instant re-bid? e.g., keep a fraction of bids at a slightly higher floor for 10-20m?

aj: exactly. idea: maintain a small hedged capacity (warm buffer) per region / instance-family and only scale price-optimized pools after smoothing window. less churn and fewer drains.

kevin: cost tradeoff? keeping warm buffer raised hourly costs. how big do you estimate buffer needs to be for our batch training workload?

aj: initial sims suggest 5-7% of baseline cluster size reduces interruption-driven queue stalls by ~60% for p3/p4 style jobs. net cost delta ~ +1.2% — seems worth it for SLAs.

maria: can we mix capacity-optimized with price-optimized instead? choose CAPACITY_FIRST in us-west, PRICE_FIRST in eu for cheaper markets?

aj: yes, mix is the plan. smoothing applied to price pools only; capacity pools act as anchoring layer. Also add cross-region failover with a cool-down to avoid thrash (i.e., don't failover for <15m windows).

sachin: concern: cross-region failover increases egress and data transfer costs for checkpoint pulls. need to ensure pinned datasets replicate or we drain jobs gracefully.

aj: agreed. for long-running training we prefer draining + resubmit in same region unless job is restartable. For short ephemeral inference batches, failover is fine. will add policy per job class.

kevin: implementation notes? where do we put smoothing logic (provisioner vs procurement agent)?

aj: implement in procurement agent upstream of autoscaler. agent keeps a short-timeseries (price + preempt prob) and exposes target bid curve to the autoscaler. autoscaler still decides node creation but follows the smoothed bid targets.

maria: can you sketch config?

aj: sample: 

```
proc_agent:
  smoothing_window: 15m  # moving window to average spot signals
  hedged_fraction: 0.06  # fraction of capacity kept as warm buffer per region
  bid_strategy:
    price_pool:
      bidding_mode: price-optimized
      bid_floor_pct: 0.6 # relative to on-demand
      bid_ceiling_pct: 0.92
    capacity_pool:
      bidding_mode: capacity-optimized
```

aj: agent will emit a prioritized region list with per-region bid targets. autoscaler respects: prefer same-region, fallback-order, and a region cooldown TTL.

ops-bot: Deploy plan created: rollout/proc-agent/temporal-smoothing v1 -> canary (5%) -> 5m -> 25% -> 30m -> 100%

kevin: how to measure success? metrics: preempt rate, mean time to reassign, average scheduling latency, cost per GPU-hour. Also track failed job restarts.

sachin: add a passive experiment: run smoothing off for 10% of traffic to measure. A/B helps validate cost/noise effects.

aj: yes will include an A/B tag on routes. Also add alerting: if smoothing increases cost >3% and doesn't reduce preempts by at least 30% in 24h -> auto rollback.

maria: one more gotcha: small regions (e.g., ap-south) have brittle capacity — hedged_fraction should be higher there. maybe scale hedged_fraction by region_stability_score.

aj: good call. region_stability_score will be a rolling 7d availability metric. when <0.75, hedged_fraction *= 2.

kevin: ok action items: aj - prototype proc-agent change + sim; maria - export region stability scores to metrics; sachin - add dataset locality flag to job spec; i'll review rollout.

aj: thanks. I'll push a prototype branch and share perf sim results by EOD Thursday.

maria: :thumbsup:

sachin: thanks, will coordinate datasets.

ops-bot: Canary deployment started for rollout/proc-agent/temporal-smoothing v1 at 1912348922

aj: noted canary start. will watch preempt-rate dash.

kevin: quick note: document the expectation of egress for cross-region cold start in the runbook (cost + time).

aj: will do.

maria: also add a playbook step: if region-wide spot storm persists >1h, switch to reserved fallback capacity and notify SRE paging.

kevin: nice. thanks team.
